answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The activation profile matches fine-tune bias almost exactly. Relative L2 at layers 1/8/16/24/32 is 0.085/0.145/0.196/0.234/0.411, against the documented 0.087/0.144/0.192/0.228/0.406. The final-layer jump is +0.108, the largest of any class (documented +0.10). Direction consistency is 0.700, effective rank 3.05, final cosine 0.908, mid-layer size ratio 1.022 and onset layer 12; the documented values are 0.701, 3.01, 0.909, 1.022 and 13–14. Quantization is ruled out by the size ratio above 1, the lower rank and the higher consistency. Fine-tune backdoor is ruled out because there is no early bump (onset 12, not 3), consistency is higher than its 0.62, and the final value is larger than its 0.30. Both system-prompt classes are ruled out by the small layer-2 spike (1.9 vs about 42) and the much smaller mid-depth difference (0.196 vs about 0.4). Output and logit levels were not available, so this rests on activations alone.
